approved_by: PI, relayed by the repository owner
what_changed: The RRCS section heading 'Complete RRCS results' became 'RRCS results', and reports whose table is capped at 1,000 rows gained one line directly below that heading: 'Showing 1,000 of N contact pairs.' The sticky-navigation label for that section changed from 'Complete RRCS' to 'RRCS results' in the same approved correction.
why: _get_complete_rrcs() caps the table at 1,000 rows, so 'Complete' overstated it for 7 of the 283 receptors.
scope: The pre-V3 baseline in freeze_manifest.json is unchanged and remains authoritative: the freeze test reverses every rule in 'reversal' below and then compares against that baseline, so any other difference still fails. The top-level 'what_changed', 'why', 'row_cap', 'ordering' and 'truncated_receptors' keys describe the first approval (2026-08-26, the sec-rrcs header). The text fixes of 2026-10-19 are documented on their own rules (each rule has an id).
ordering: delta_df.nlargest(1000, 'abs_delta'): the 1,000 contact pairs with the largest |ΔRRCS|, descending. Ties broken by pandas' nlargest, which keeps first occurrence in row order.

reversal.why: The link pointed at Heo and Feig's paper (doi 10.1002/prot.26382) but the text named "del Alamo et al., 2022".
reversal.after: rel="noopener">Heo L, Feig M. Proteins 2022;90(11):1873-1885, doi 10.1002/prot.26382)

reversal.what: Every place a report names the gnomAD release (Methods link text, the Allele freq and Het count column tooltips, the Understanding paragraph).
reversal.why: The variants were fetched from gnomAD v4.1 (dataset gnomad_r4) on 2026-02-02; "gnomAD v4" did not name the release.

reversal.what: Citation after the gnomAD credit in Methods.
reversal.why: Methods credited gnomAD without citing it.

reversal.what: Citation and licence line after the AlphaMissense credit in Methods.
reversal.why: Methods credited AlphaMissense with no citation and no licence; the Studio states the predictions as CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
reversal.after: >AlphaMissense (Cheng et al., Science 2023; predictions licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0);

reversal.why: The conservation scores are VarSite scores served by ProtVar; "ProtVar / UniProt" named the wrong source pair.
reversal.after: conservation from VarSite scores served by ProtVar (Stephenson et al., Nucleic Acids Res 2024, doi 10.1093/nar/gkae413).
reversal.before: conservation from ProtVar / UniProt.

reversal.what: The Het count sentence in Methods.
reversal.why: It said homozygote counts are uniformly zero. They are not: 789 of the 29,213 alleles in the site's variant tables (3,621 of 145,345 alleles in the Studio's full gnomAD v4.1 pack) have ac_hom > 0. het_count = ac - 2 * ac_hom for every row.
reversal.after: The Het count column shows heterozygote allele counts (allele count minus twice the homozygote count); homozygote counts are not shown.
reversal.before: The Het count column shows heterozygote allele counts; homozygote counts are uniformly zero across these rare missense variants in the current gnomAD v4 snapshot and are omitted.

reversal.what: Citations for GPCRdb and UniProt in the Structural annotation paragraph (UniProt moves here from the conservation credit).
reversal.why: Methods credited GPCRdb and UniProt without citing them.
reversal.after: >GPCRdb (Herrera et al., Nucleic Acids Res 2025, doi 10.1093/nar/gkae1065); protein accessions from UniProt (The UniProt Consortium, Nucleic Acids Res 2025, doi 10.1093/nar/gkae1010).

section_nav_labels.why_pinned_here: data-section-title sits on the section's OPENING tag, and the freeze scope is the inner HTML excluding that tag. The content hash therefore cannot see these labels, and the reversal rules above cannot guard them. tests/test_report_nav_labels.py pins them instead, so an unrelated label edit still fails.
section_nav_labels.optional_reason: The 4 receptors absent from the variant dataset render no variants section, so that label is absent for them.
